podcast.title: Hair Metal Endeavors (1988)
podcast.body: In 1988, Ondrasik became involved with the hair metal scene, playing in glammy hair metal bands alongside musicians like Rudy Sarzo (Whitesnake's bass player), securing management deals before the rise of Grunge. "In 1988 he fell in with some hair metal guys including Rudy Sarso, the bass player for White Snake."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Breakthrough at 34
podcast.body: John Ondrasik achieved his major breakthrough at age 34 with the success of his album *America Town* and its single "Superman," marking a long journey to his first hit. "It was John's breakthrough at age 34."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Early Musical Training
podcast.body: John Ondrasik initially pursued music, taking piano lessons, learning to sing opera, and songwriting, before pursuing a degree in Applied Science and Math at UCLA as a backup career. "He took piano lessons, learned to sing opera and dabbled in songwriting."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Impact of Grunge (Age 25)
podcast.body: At age 25, his aspirations of becoming a hair metal superstar were cut short by the advent of Grunge music. "But then Grunge came along and just like that at age 25, John's hopes of being a hair metal superstar were dead."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Return to Piano and Solo Gigs
podcast.body: After the decline of hair metal, John Ondrasik returned to playing piano and performing at small gigs across Los Angeles, not wanting to spend his days doing math. "John went back to the piano and started playing small gigs around Los Angeles."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Origin of Name
xref.body: John Ondrasik adopted the name "Five for Fighting" as a hockey reference, and because record company personnel struggled to pronounce his last name. "And he picked that name because no record company person could pronounce his last name."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
